method: direct Wright-Fisher / coalescent simulation, pure stdlib python3.12 on MSI acn112, 16 cores; every null preceded by a positive control

positive_controls.P1_mutation_drift_identity: single WF population, infinite alleles: measured Q vs EXACT discrete fixed point (1-mu)^2/(2Ne) / (1-(1-mu)^2(1-1/(2Ne))). theta=0.25 +0.40%, theta=1 +1.82%, theta=4 -0.03%. PASS (640 replicates each)

findings_ranked.verdict: REGIME UNSTATED / DOCSTRING UNDERSPECIFIED; numerically WRONG for the standard split
findings_ranked.simulation: two isolated WF demes, Ne=100, infinite alleles, 320 replicates, Fst=(Qs-Qb)/(1-Qb)
findings_ranked.why: the Lean rate constant (1+theta)/(2Ne) = 2mu + 1/(2Ne) is the relaxation rate of the WITHIN-deme identity Qs, not of Fst. After an isolating split, lineages in different demes can never coalesce, so Qb has only one clock, mutation, at rate 2mu = theta/(2Ne). The two rates differ by (1+theta)/theta, which diverges as theta -> 0 (=5x at theta=0.25).
findings_ranked.derived_correct_form_for_equilibrium_spl: Fst(t) = Q*(1-x)/(1 - Q* x) with x=(1-mu)^(2t), Q* the mutation-drift identity
findings_ranked.note: The Lean body IS correct for a split from an ancestor with zero within-population identity, which is a legitimate but non-standard idealisation. The docstring's 'Starting from Fst=0' is true of both initial conditions and does not select one.

findings_ranked.docstring_claim: the fraction of LD that decays per generation is 1/(2Ne)
findings_ranked.verdict: DOCSTRING NUMERICALLY WRONG (definition body is a bare rate and survives; the reading attached to it does not)
findings_ranked.evidence: the same file's ldRetentionPerGen r Ne = (1-r)(1-1/(2Ne)) is VALIDATED to 0.7% by fam_ld_decay.py. The fraction of E[D] lost per generation is therefore 1-(1-r)(1-1/(2Ne)) = r + 1/(2Ne) - r/(2Ne), exact rational arithmetic:
findings_ranked.note: same defect class, same file, as the already-REPAIRED ldHalfLife (2110x) and ldRetainedFraction (37000x): the recombination argument is absent, so the r=0 slice is the only place the claim holds. Unbounded in r/(1/(2Ne)).

findings_ranked.verdict: DOCSTRING OVERCLAIMS; the body is not a fraction of anything
findings_ranked.evidence: the exponent is, by the corpus's own composition, a COUNT of mutations. Simulation (SIM4) measures that count: 599.9 arisen at theta=1,t=1200, so the body evaluates to exp(-600) = 1e-261, and 2423.8 at theta=4, giving exp(-2424). A quantity described as 'the fraction of LD that is shared between populations' is identically 0 to machine precision for any locus older than roughly 60/theta generations.
findings_ranked.note: no simulation is needed to see the scale problem, but SIM4 supplies the count the exponent actually is. Nothing in the corpus derives an exp(-N_mutations) law; the plausible-looking regime (theta t/2 ~ 1) exists only for per-SITE theta and vanishes for any locus-scale theta.

findings_ranked.verdict: BODY CORRECT as a count of mutations ARISING; DOCSTRING'S SECOND SENTENCE WRONG
findings_ranked.why: the docstring says 'Over t generations, the expected number of new SEGREGATING SITES is ~theta t/2'. Segregating sites saturate at Watterson's theta*sum(1/i), which the simulation reproduces to 2-3%; theta t/2 grows without bound. Overstatement 118x at t=1200 and growing linearly in t.

findings_ranked.verdict: CONFIRMS the corpus's own recorded defect, independently and at a different lattice size
findings_ranked.simulation: direct two-lineage Monte Carlo, circle D=64, Ne=25, m=0.2, sigma^2=1, 48000 replicates per d
findings_ranked.note: the corpus records the factor as (D-d) measured at D=256; at D=64 the measured factors are 73/58/32 against (D-d)=63/56/32. Confirmed.

findings_ranked.verdict: NUMERICALLY CORRECT (VERIFIED); the case-only d/D collision is a live, uncaught hazard
findings_ranked.simulation_agreement: measured/predicted = 1.026 at d=4, 1.027 at d=8, 1.006 at d=16, 1.004 at d=32; 1.163 at d=1 (lattice discreteness at one step)
findings_ranked.call_site_audit: the only consumers in the corpus are steppingStoneMeetingTime_eq_scaled and steppingStoneMeetingTime_eq_perDeme_iff (DemographicHistory.lean:264,276) and differential/checks.py:641. No call site currently swaps them.
findings_ranked.swap_is_detectable: a d<->D swap always flips the sign (d < D), so it yields a NEGATIVE expected time. Nothing in the corpus rules this out: there is no nonnegativity or positivity theorem for steppingStoneMeetingTimeOnLattice, unlike its siblings. That theorem is the cheap guard.
findings_ranked.second_and_worse_collision: sigma_sq and m enter only as the product 2*sigma_sq*m, so a sigma_sq <-> m swap is EXACTLY invisible -- no test, simulation, or theorem can ever detect it. And the two siblings order them oppositely in the same file: demoSteppingStoneFst (d Ne m sigma_sq) vs steppingStoneDiffusionTimescale (d sigma_sq m) vs steppingStoneMeetingTimeOnLattice (d D sigma_sq m). demoSteppingStoneFst is likewise symmetric in m and sigma_sq. This is the higher-risk collision of the two.

findings_ranked.verdict: HYPERBOLIC FORM VERIFIED by direct simulation, independently of the corpus's own solver; the exponential is confirmed beaten; the d << D regime bound is confirmed and quantified
findings_ranked.simulation: two-lineage stepping-stone coalescent run forward as a process (lineages walk, coalesce with prob 1/(2Ne) when co-located), circle D=64, Ne=25, m=0.2, sigma^2=1; Fst = 1 - T_within/T_between
findings_ranked.note: the deletion of continuousSteppingStoneFst is corroborated: the exponential, with L FITTED freely to the measurement, is 1.8x worse than the corpus form in the corpus form's own stated regime. Replacing d by d(D-d)/D -- the same coalescent derivation without the d << D truncation -- removes essentially all of the far-field error (0.1715 -> 0.0612) and is the form the corpus does not carry.
findings_ranked.second_order_finding: the two compensating omissions the corpus documents are confirmed quantitatively. Measured T_within = 3136.9 = 2*D*Ne, NOT the per-deme 2*Ne = 50 that coalFst is handed -- a factor of 64 (=D). It cancels against the (D-d)~D dropped from the meeting time, which is exactly why demoSteppingStoneFst is right anyway.

findings_ranked.simulation: n=20 deme island model, Ne=25, infinite-alleles mutation, time-averaged equilibrium Fst=(Qs-Qb)/(1-Qb), 16 independent replicates x 4000 sampled generations after 1500 burn-in
findings_ranked.note: the residual is monotone in 4Nm and is fully accounted for by the finite-deme island correction (n/(n-1))^2 at n=20, which the definition legitimately omits as an infinite-island idealisation. Non-vacuous: Fst spans 0.17-0.57 over the grid and the additivity of the two rates is separately exercised by the (4Nm=1, theta=0.5) vs (4Nm=1, theta=2) pair.

findings_ranked.verdict: VERIFIED CORRECT -- this is the clean finding
findings_ranked.simulation: 3.2 million simulated admixed haplotypes per cell, ancestry drawn per haplotype then alleles drawn independently within source
findings_ranked.note: grid includes a negative-D cell (alpha=0.8, dp1<0), so a sign or argument-order error separates. Controls P4 (dp1=0 and dp2=0) return -0.00012 and -0.00020 against exactly 0.

not_reached.Descent.LDDecayTheory.driftLDStep: UNTESTED, LDDecayTheory.lean:263. Not reached by direct simulation. Reason: the Sved Q is a DEFECTIVE identity (IBD with no intervening recombination on either lineage); a plain forward label simulation measures ordinary two-locus IBD, which goes to 1 with no mutation and is a different quantity, so the naive direct simulation would have tested the wrong thing. A correct direct test needs an ancestral-recombination-graph simulation, which I did not have time to build.
not_reached.Descent.LDDecayTheory.driftLDRetention: UNTESTED, LDDecayTheory.lean:285. Same reason; it is the slope of driftLDStep.
